summary: After small rural schools merged or closed, some children faced much longer bus rides and some parents were paid to drive them.
realLife: Vermont Public described the effects of about 40 school mergers across the state. In one district students ride up to an hour and a half, and one boy's ride was set to more than double if his middle school closed. A road on one route was closed about a dozen times by washouts and accidents. One district found a bus too costly and paid parents $300 a month to drive children about 12 miles over a mountain road. Parents who work long hours may not be able to drive, so the burden is uneven.
sources: https://www.vermontpublic.org/post/lot-road-cover-schools-close-some-kids-face-longer-bus-rides (Vermont Public on school mergers and bus rides)
gates: the new school is in another town
the household's parents work long hours

turns.what: The child boards earlier and gets home later, and the parent loses time with school activities.
turns.pulledBy: a merger that moves the school out of town

turns.what: A parent with a flexible job drives and takes a stipend that covers some fuel.
turns.pulledBy: a stipend and a job that bends

turns.what: A vote or a withdrawal keeps the school and the ride stays short.
